Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.name: Sag
params.description: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.

params.description: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Bass
params.description: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Level
params.description: Controls the overall level of the Preamp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.

params.name: Hum
params.description: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.name: Level

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.

params.name: Hum
params.description: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Increasing this parameter attenuates high frequencies, effectively reducing the amp's brightness.

params.name: Hype
params.description: Depending on the amp and/or amp settings, increasing Hype may subtly or dramatically adjust various behind-the-scenes parameters to make the amp sound and feel smoother, fuller, punchier, tighter, and/or more forgiving, but at the expense of accuracy.

params.name: Level
params.description: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.

params.name: Master
params.description: Controls the Master Volume of the amplifier.

params.name: Normal Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of Normal channel gain applied to the signal. The inactive channel can sometimes "bleed into" the active channel, resulting in interesting interactions.

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.name: Sag
params.description: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.

params.name: Treble
params.description: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Z PrePost
params.description: Determines the location of speaker impedance characteristics in the power amp, primarily due to negative feedback. Higher values mean the effects of the interaction appear at the output of the power amp (Post) and lower values mean more of the effect is fed back to the input of the power amp (Pre).

params.name: Bass
params.description: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Bias
params.description: Adjusts the bias of the tubes in the power amp, causing a change in tonality and the distortion characteristic.

params.name: Bias X
params.description: Determines how the power amp tubes’ voicing reacts when pushed hard. Set low for a tighter feel. Set high for more tube compression. This parameter is highly reactive with the Drive and Master settings.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.

params.name: Hum
params.description: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

Higher values mean the effects of the interaction appear at the output of the power amp (Post) and lower values mean more of the effect is fed back to the input of the power amp (Pre).

params.name: Bass
params.description: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Bias
params.description: Adjusts the bias of the tubes in the power amp, causing a change in tonality and the distortion characteristic.

params.name: Bias X
params.description: Determines how the power amp tubes’ voicing reacts when pushed hard. Set low for a tighter feel. Set high for more tube compression. This parameter is highly reactive with the Drive and Master settings.

params.name: Boost
params.description: When set to "High," boosts the preamp's gain.

params.name: Level
params.description: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.

params.name: Class
params.description: Selects the power amp class--A or A/B. Class A generally sounds a bit richer and more compressed while Class A/B exhibits greater punch with better note separation and additional headroom.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.

params.name: Depth
params.description: This 3-position switch sets the amount of damping. "Tight" maintains balance between the low and high strings, "Loose" provides a notable bass boost, and "Medium" is somewhere in the middle.

params.name: Master
params.description: Controls the master volume of the amplifier.

params.name: Mid
params.description: Controls the midrange frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Style
params.description: When set to "Triode," 3 out of 5 elements in the tubes are active, which can sound a bit smoother. When set to "Pentode," all tube elements are active, which provides more bite and punch.

params.name: Bright
params.description: Adds two levels of brightness before the tonestack--B1 and B2.

params.name: Presence
params.description: Boosts upper mid and high frequencies in the power amp, resulting in additional punch and bite.

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.name: Sag
params.description: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.

params.name: Structure
params.description: Adjusts the amount and texture of distortion, providing a subtle EQ shift.

params.name: Bright
params.description: Engages one of two different values of bright capacitor, and is more pronounced at lower Drive settings. When Drive is at 10.0, Bright is effectively removed from the amp circuit.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.

params.name: FET Boost
params.description: Provides a 7-9 dB FET (Field Effect Transistor) boost and tweaks the EQ a bit. The result is similar to placing a FET boost pedal before the amp.

params.name: Hum
params.description: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.name: Jazz Rock
params.description: Changes the tonestack's wiring, allowing for two totally separate tonal voices. Jazz is quieter with a lower center frequency for the mids. Rock is louder with a more traditional mid frequency center. Tone controls rarely translate well between the Jazz and Rock settings. If a good sound is achieved in one mode, it is not guaranteed that the same settings in the opposite mode will still sound pleasing.

params.name: Master
params.description: Controls the master volume of the amplifier. It is located between the preamp and power amp and can be used to get more or less power amp distortion. This amp is VERY loud, and if the Master is cranked, the power amp distortion can be pushed into unpleasant territory.

params.name: Mid
params.description: Controls the midrange frequency EQ of the tonestack. NOTE: Voicing changes with the Jazz Rock switch.

params.name: Mid Switch
params.description: Changes the value of the treble capacitor in the tone stack. When off, the amp has more of a scooped sound; when on, there is a noticeable upper-mid boost.

params.name: OD Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of drive or saturation in the overdrive circuit. Since the whole overdrive circuit is after the amp's regular Drive and Tone controls, the range of OD Drive will change based on those earlier knob settings.

params.name: OD Level
params.description: Controls the output level of the overdrive circuit.

params.name: OD Switch
params.description: Turns the two-gain-stage tube overdrive circuit on and off. This circuit is located AFTER the tone controls and Drive knob. When the overdrive is turned on it's as if third and fourth gain stages are added to the preamp.

params.name: PAB
params.description: Adds a preamp boost between tube stages 1 and 2, but at the expense of removing the tonestack controls from the circuit.

params.name: Presence
params.description: Boosts high frequencies in the power amp by modifying the EQ filtering in the power amp's negative feedback loop.

Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Adjusts the overall tonal character of the amplifier, allowing you to emphasize either the bass or treble frequencies.

params.name: Treble
params.description: Controls the high frequency EQ of the tonestack. The original amp didn't have a Treble knob; set to 5.0 for accurate response.

params.name: Bass
params.description: Controls the low frequency EQ of the tonestack.

params.name: Bias
params.description: Adjusts the bias of the tubes in the power amp, causing a change in tonality and the distortion characteristic.

params.name: Bias X
params.description: Determines how the power amp tubes’ voicing reacts when pushed hard. Set low for a tighter feel. Set high for more tube compression. This parameter is highly reactive with the Drive and Master settings.

params.name: Level
params.description: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion. At higher settings, things get gnarly.

params.name: Hum
params.description: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.name: Master
params.description: Controls the Master Volume of the amplifier.

params.name: Mid
params.description: Controls the midrange frequency EQ of the tonestack. The original amp didn't have a Mid knob; set to 5.0 for accurate response.

params.name: Presence
params.description: Boosts upper mid and high frequencies in the power amp, resulting in additional punch and bite.

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.description: Controls the overall level of the Amp block. Unlike Master Volume, it has no effect on the block's tone.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal, which influences the level of distortion.

params.name: Hum
params.description: Adjusts the level of power supply hum that interacts with the signal. Preamp tube heaters in tube amps will leak a little bit of 60 cycle hum into the audio signal. When this hum mixes with the distorted audio signal, a non-musical distortion is created at low levels. To some players, this low-level, non-harmonic distortion adds a bit of realism to the amp model.

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. params.name: Hype

params.name: Mid

params.name: Normal Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of Normal channel gain applied to the signal. The inactive channel can sometimes "bleed into" the active channel, resulting in interesting interactions.

params.name: Presence
params.description: Boosts upper mid and high frequencies in the power amp, resulting in additional punch and bite.

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. params.name: Sag

params.name: Treble

params.name: Z PrePost

params.name: Ripple
params.description: Controls how much AC ripple interacts with your tone. Power amp circuits will sometimes let a little bit of rectified 120Hz hum (that the power supply filter caps can't quite fully remove) into the audio signal when the power supply is being pushed hard. Much like Hum, Ripple provides a bit of non-musical distortion to the power amp at distorted settings.

params.name: Sag
params.description: Controls the amount of sag, or how much the power supply compresses or "droops" in response to striking the strings hard. Higher values provide more touch dynamics, sustain, and organic feel that's inherent in vintage tube amps; lower values offer a "tighter" responsiveness for a more modern feel.

For pedals like distortion, fuzz, or compression, it's common to keep the FX Loop's Mix knob at 100% so the entire signal is effected, although parallel processing can be accomplished at lower values.

params.description: Adjusts the amount of dry signal through the Feedbacker block.

params.description: Determines the type of the feedback generated. For Mid to Low (or High to Low), feedback starts on the highest harmonic below 500 Hz (or 1200 Hz) and descends to lower harmonics. Rndm Onset harmonics are selected randomly every time a new note or chord is detected. Rndm Trigger harmonics are selected randomly every time Retrigger is set to "Trigger."

params.name: Feedback Gain
params.description: Controls the amount of feedback. At higher settings, can easily overwhelm your guitar signal; at lower settings, the feedback can better "sit" between chords. WARNING! Be careful, as this effect can quickly go off the rails, just like real feedback. Consider assigning it to a momentary stomp so feedback only appears while you hold the switch.

params.name: Offset Thresh
params.description: Rapid drops in the signal level by this amount will quickly kill the feedback to prevent warbling.

params.name: Onset Thresh
params.description: When Feedback Type is set to Rndm Offset, sets the threshold of onsets (plucks) that cause changes to the feedback note. Lower values increase sensitivity to plucking and strumming and higher values reduce sensitivity.

params.name: Reference
params.description: Determines which note within a chord is referenced by the feedback. "Lowest" prioritizes a chord's lowest-pitched note while "Loudest" prioritizes the loudest note in the chord.

params.name: Release
params.description: Controls how quickly each harmonic dies out or transitions to a different one. At higher values, you may hear more than one harmonic as they transition.

params.name: Retrigger
params.description: Meant to be assigned to a Stomp switch. Every time you press the switch, the feedback changes, depending on the type of mode: Mid to Low or High to Low-Feedback descends to lower harmonics. Rndm Trigger or Rndm Offset-Feedback randomly chooses a different harmonic. All other modes-Feedback regenerates at the mode's selected frequency.

params.name: Silence Thresh
params.description: Adjusts the level threshold above which feedback is generated. Below this level, no feedback is generated.

params.name: Trails
params.description: Determines whether feedback continues to ring out (for the duration of the Release parameter) after the block is bypassed.

params.name: Intensity
params.description: Controls the amplitude of the modulation, from mild to deep.

With Sine, 50% is a normal sine wave and extreme values warp the wave toward a parabolic down (0%) or parabolic up (100%) shape. With Square, 50% is an even square wave, higher values lengthen the signal's on time, and lower values shorten the signal's on time. DutyCycle does not apply to Saw Up or Saw down.

params.name: Treble Freq
params.description: Sets the lower range of the high frequency band. Harmonic Tremolo modulates between the low and high frequency bands.

params.name: Wave Shape
params.description: Selects the wave shape of the tremolo. Classic tremolo is commonly a sine or triangle wave, but cool choppy sounds can be discovered with square or saw down waves.

params.name: Voice 1 Scale
params.description: Voice/harmony 1's delay time is always some percentage of the root note's time (controlled via Time), and is determined by the V1 Scale parameter. For example, if Time is set to 800 ms and V1 Scale is set to 75%, voice/harmony 1's delay is 600 ms (or 75% of 800 ms). When scale is set to 100%, voice/harmony 1 and root delays are the same.

params.name: Voice 2 Scale
params.description: Voice/harmony 2's delay time is always some percentage of the root note's time (controlled via Time), and is determined by the V2 Scale parameter. For example, if Time is set to 800 ms and V2 Scale is set to 25%, voice/harmony 2's delay is 200 ms (or 25% of 800 ms). When scale is set to 100%, voice/harmony 2 and root delays are the same.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Feedback controls the number of repeated pitch sequences. When set to 0%, the two voice/harmony repeats are heard only once, followed by the root note again. At higher values, the three note sequence (root, voice/harmony 1, and voice/harmony 2) cycle repeatedly.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Voice 1 Shift
params.description: Selects voice/harmony 1's note in the specified Key. For example, if Key is set to "D" and Scale is set to "Minor" (which I always find is the saddest of all keys), setting V1 Shift to +3 will repeat an F (or the third note above D in the D minor scale).

params.name: Voice 2 Shift
params.description: Selects voice/harmony 2's note in the specified Key. For example, if Key is set to "D" and Scale is set to "Minor" (which I always find is the saddest of all keys), setting V2 Shift to -2 will repeat a Bb (or the second note below D in the D minor scale).

params.name: Key
params.description: Along with Scale, specifies the scale reference for V1 Shift and V2 Shift values. For example, if you choose D Minor and then PLAY IN D MINOR (Harmony Delay can't fix bad notes), V1 Shift and V2 Shift will always shift your repeats to pitches in that scale.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Root Level
params.description: Controls the level of the root (unpitched) repeats. If you only want to hear the harmony repeats, set Root Level to 0.0.

params.name: Voice 1 Level
params.description: Controls the level of the voice/harmony 1 repeats.

params.name: Voice 2 Level
params.description: Controls the level of the voice/harmony 2 repeats.

params.name: Mix

params.name: Root Pan

params.name: Voice 2 Pan

params.name: Scale
params.description: Along with Key, specifies the scale reference for V1 Shift and V2 Shift values. For example, if you choose D Minor and then PLAY IN D MINOR (Harmony Delay can't fix wrong notes), V1 Shift and V2 Shift will shift your repeats to pitches in that scale.

params.name: Time

params.name: Gain

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of the distortion. Lower values are darker and higher values are brighter.

params.name: Clipping
params.description: Selects the clipping mode. "Overdrive" has a touch of drive and compression. "Clean" is less compressed than "Overdrive" and is ideal for boosting your signal into an amp. "Distortion" provides even more drive and compression.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Controls the amount of gain applied to the signal.

params.name: Gain Mod
params.description: The original pedal has different variations available, one with more gain ("Higher").

params.name: Level

params.name: Presence

params.name: Tone

params.name: Voltage
params.description: The original pedal was designed to be powered by a 9V power supply but could alternatively accommodate 18V, which would provide a bit more headroom. This is especially apparent when Clipping is set to "Boost" and Gain is turned up.

params.name: Depth
params.description: Controls the depth or amount of modulation.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard.

params.name: Headroom
params.description: Some delay pedals' internal signal paths exhibit a bit of grit, especially when placed after a high-gain amp block. Negative values increase the perceived amount of grit; positive values clean things up a bit.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix

params.name: Attack

params.name: Bright
params.description: Controls the brightness of the signal, but acts more like a traditional tone knob. Turn up if your amp is muddy or dark; turn down if the high end appears a bit strident or harsh.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of distortion, saturation, and sustain.

params.name: Gate
params.description: Controls the sensitivity of the dynamic high shelf EQ filter. Lower values eliminate most noise without affecting your tone; higher values can tighten up your bass response, at the expense of note articulation.

params.name: Gate Range
params.description: Determines the range of the dynamic high shelf EQ filter, or how far the signal is attenuated while the gate is active. When set to "Extended," drops the gate's threshold down to -90 dB, which is more attenuation than the real pedal.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Gate Range

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mode
params.description: Determines whether the gate's response is optimized for bass or guitar.

params.name: Sensitivity
params.description: Lower values eliminate most noise without affecting your tone; higher values can tighten up your bass response, at the expense of note articulation. Note that Horizon Gate isn't a traditional gate as much as it's a dynamic high shelf EQ filter that squashes high end noise while letting lower end signals continue to decay naturally.

params.name: Drip
params.description: Adjusts the intensity of the spring reverb, or how much "ploink" you might hear.

params.name: Dwell
params.description: Controls the strength of the signal sent into the spring tank. Higher values result in a longer decay.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the reverb and the dry signal. At 0%, no reverb is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Spring Count
params.description: Selects how many springs are in the tank (1, 2, or 3, and numerous values in between).

params.name: Compress
params.description: The Compress knob doesn't actually control a compressor, it controls the pedal's transistor bias. However, higher values can pinch the dynamics of the signal, much like a compressor.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Adjusts the amount of fuzz applied to the signal. Becomes less effective as Comp is turned up.

params.name: Gate
params.description: Higher values can squelch your sustain, like a gate, but it's more spitty and nasty than a gate, not that there's anything wrong with that.

params.name: Level

params.name: Oscillator
params.description: Turns the oscillator on and off.

params.name: Stability
params.description: Controls the amount of voltage the pedal sees. Lower settings can slightly soften or mellow out the fuzz.

params.name: Asymmetry
params.description: Adjusts the amount of clipping symmetry. Lower values are more symmetrical; higher values are more asymmetrical, or more "broken." More audible when running into a clean amp.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Controls the amount of distortion applied to the signal.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Pull Diode
params.description: Selects the type of clipping diode for the second socket. The original pedal's circuit included sockets so the user could swap out diodes to customize their sound.

params.name: Push Diode
params.description: Selects the type of clipping diode for the first socket. The original pedal's circuit included sockets so the user could swap out diodes to customize their sound.

params.name: Treble
params.description: Controls the high frequency EQ of the distortion.

params.name: Boost
params.description: Adds a 3dB boost to the signal via a virtual dip switch.

params.name: Bright
params.description: Adds additional brightness via a virtual dip switch.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of drive applied to the signal.

params.name: Attack
params.description: Controls how quickly compression responds to increases in input signal level. Higher values mean a slower attack, which lets the instrument's initial transient sneak through and only compresses the sustained portion of the signal.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the compressed and dry signals. At 0%, no compressed signal is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. Values in between provide parallel compression.

params.name: Release
params.description: Controls how quickly the signal returns to unity gain after it falls below the threshold.

params.name: Sensitivity
params.description: Controls the sensitivity of the compressor's input. Higher values apply more compression.

params.name: Body
params.description: Adds body resonance, which can provide additional fullness or fatness.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mode
params.description: Selects one of four acoustic guitar sounds: Standard is a traditional acoustic guitar, Jumbo is larger and fuller, Enhanced has a more prominent attack for cutting through a mix, and Piezo approximates the sound of a piezo pickup installed on the guitar.

params.name: Shimmer
params.description: Imparts some motion to the harmonics, reminiscent of how a string's vibration tends to affect the other strings.

params.name: Top
params.description: Accentuates higher end string attack and harmonics.

params.name: Emphasis
params.description: Subtly increases the compression circuit's sensitivity to high frequencies. At 0.0, no emphasis is applied.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Increases the signal's level to compensate for the reduced level that results from compression/peak reduction.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the compressed and dry signals. At 0%, no compressed signal is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. Values in between provide parallel compression.

params.name: Peak Reduction
params.description: Peak Reduction lowers the threshold, controlling how much compression is applied to the input signal.

params.name: Type
params.description: Switches between compression (3:1 ratio) and limiting (Infinity:1 ratio).

params.name: Range
params.description: Frequency range of the filter

params.description: Controls how long it takes for the filter to sweep down (the Attack stage) before sweeping back up (the Release stage). Lower values result in a longer downward filter sweep. Is somewhat interactive with the Sensitivity parameter.

params.name: Frequency
params.description: Sets the highest frequency in the filter sweep. Higher values are more extreme.

params.name: Low Cut Enable

params.name: Low Cut Slope
params.description: Adjusts the slope of the Low Cut filter. Higher values apply a steeper slope.

params.name: Low Enable
params.description: Turns the Low band on and off.

params.name: Low Freq
params.description: Adjusts the frequency of the Low Band

params.name: Low Gain
params.description: Adjusts the gain of the Low band.

params.name: Low Q
params.description: Adjusts the bandwidth of the Low band. Lower values apply a wider boost or cut for shaping overall frequency response; higher values apply a precise, surgical boost or cut for accentuating a specific frequency, removing troublesome resonances, or even controlling feedback.

params.name: Low Shelf Enable
params.description: Turns the Low Shelf band on and off.

params.name: Low Shelf Freq
params.description: Adjusts the frequency of the Low Shelf band.

params.name: Low Shelf Gain
params.description: Adjusts the gain of the Low Shelf band.

params.name: Mid Enable
params.description: Turns the Mid band on and off.

params.name: Mid Freq
params.description: Adjusts the frequency for the Mid band.

params.name: Mid Gain
params.description: Adjusts the gain of the Mid band.

params.name: Mid Q
params.description: Adjusts the bandwidth of the Mid band. Lower values apply a wider boost or cut for shaping overall frequency response; higher values apply a precise, surgical boost or cut for accentuating a specific frequency, removing troublesome resonances, or even controlling feedback.

params.name: Color
params.description: When turned on, results in a more pronounced phase shifting effect.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Rate
params.description: Controls the speed or rate of the phaser. When set to note values, Speed follows the system tempo.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Controls the amount of distortion.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall output level of the block.

params.name: Mode
params.description: Chooses the type of clipping circuit. 1 is LED, 2 is Clean Op-amp, 3 is Asymmetrical.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of the distortion. Lower values are darker and higher values are brighter.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Scale
params.description: For stereo delays, the right side's time is always some percentage of the left sides's time, and is determined by the Scale parameter. For example, if Time is set to 500 ms, and Scale is set to 70%, the left delay is 500 ms and the right delay is 350ms (or 70% of 500 ms). When scale is set to 100%, left and right delays are the same.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Controls the apparent stereo width of the repeats between the left and right channels.

params.name: Time
params.description: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.

params.name: Cents
params.description: Sets the fine pitch shift of the initial repeat and if Feedback is sufficient, the shifting of each subsequent repeat.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Feedback controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard, which is perfect for a simple harmony appearing slightly after your playing (set by the Time parameter). Higher values cause the pitch change to feed back into itself, generating a cascading army of pitched echoes.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Interval
params.description: Sets the interval of the initial repeat and if Feedback is sufficient, the transposition of each subsequent repeat.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Time
params.description: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.

params.name: Duty Cycle
params.description: Alters the oscillator wave shape in differing ways. For example, when Shape is a triangle wave (5.0), 50% is a normal triangle wave and extreme values warp the wave toward a saw down (0%) or saw up (100%) shape. Or when Shape is a square wave (10.0), 50% is symmetrical and extreme values result in a wave shape that's mostly low (0%) or mostly high (100%).

params.name: FM Amount
params.description: Controls the amount of the FM (Frequency Modulation) modulator applied to the AM carrier. At 0.0, only the AM carrier is applied; at 10.0 the AM carrier is fully modulated by the FM modulator.

params.name: FM Duty
params.description: Alters the FM oscillator wave shape. 50% is symmetrical and extreme values result in a wave shape that's mostly low (0%) or mostly high (100%).

params.name: FM Octave
params.description: The frequency of the FM carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. FM Octave shifts the FM carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 3 octaves up or down.

params.name: FM Pitch
params.description: The frequency of the FM carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. FM Pitch shifts the FM carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 12.0 semitones up or down.

params.name: FM Shape
params.description: Controls the shape of the oscillator used for FM of the AM carrier. The oscillator is a sine wave at 0.0, a triangle wave at 5.0, and a square wave at 10.0.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the ring modulation, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the ring modulation, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the ring modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Octave
params.description: The frequency of the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. Octave shifts the AM carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 3 octaves up or down.

params.name: Pitch
params.description: The frequency of the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier follows the pitch of the input signal. Pitch shifts the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier in relation to the input signal by up to 12.0 semitones up or down.

params.name: Shape
params.description: Controls the shape of the main oscillator used for the AM (Amplitude Modulation) carrier. The oscillator is a sine wave at 0.0, a triangle wave at 5.0, and a square wave at 10.0.

params.name: Heel Pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch when the pedal/controller is in its lowest position.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the pitch-shifted signal and the dry signal. At 0%, no pitch-shifted signal is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Position
params.description: Adjusts the position of the controller. By default, this is assigned to Expression Pedal 1.

params.name: Toe Pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch when the pedal/controller is in its highest position.

params.name: Depth
params.description: Controls the depth or intensity of the modulation.

params.name: Headroom
params.description: Some chorus pedals' internal signal paths exhibit a bit of grit, especially when placed after a high-gain amp block. Negative values increase the perceived amount of grit; positive values clean things up a bit.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no modulation is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Mode
params.description: Selects the type of modulation--Chorus or Vibrato.

params.name: Rate
params.description: Controls the speed or rate of the chorus/vibrato. When set to note values, Rate follows the system tempo.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of the modulation.

params.name: Cents 1
params.description: Adjusts the first pitch-shifter in cents, from -50 to +50

params.name: Cents 2
params.description: Adjusts the second pitch-shifter in cents, from -50 to +50.

params.name: Decay
params.description: Adjusts the decay time of the reverb effect.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the reverb and the dry signal. At 0%, no reverb is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Modulation
params.description: Controls the amount of modulation applied to the reverb.

params.name: Pitch 1
params.description: Adjusts the first pitch-shifter in semitones, from 2 octaves down to 2 octaves up.

params.name: Pitch 2
params.description: Adjusts the second pitch-shifter in semitones, from 2 octaves down to 2 octaves up.

params.name: Pitch Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the pitch-shifted signal and dry signal sent to the reverb.

params.name: Predelay
params.description: Controls the amount of delay heard before the audible onset of reverb. Can sometimes result in more definition between the dry and effected signals.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Controls the tonal balance of the reverb. Lower values are darker, higher values are brighter.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the amount of signal sent through the FX Loop. When connecting time-based pedals like delays or reverbs, it's best to leave the pedal's Mix at 100% and control the amount of the pedal's effect from the FX Loop block's Mix knob; this helps minimize phase issues and latency. For pedals like distortion, fuzz, or compression, it's common to keep the FX Loop's Mix knob at 100% so the entire signal is effected, although parallel processing can be accomplished at lower values.

If the effected signal sounds too harsh when pitched up (or dull when pitched down), adjust this setting to taste. The higher the value, the more EQ is applied at the shift end points; when set to 0.0, no compensation EQ is applied.

params.description: Determines how the poly pitch engine reacts to your playing. Leave this set to "X Stable" (fewest artifacts when pitch shifting complex chords) and only select a different setting if you experience too much latency when playing fast lead lines.

params.name: Blend
params.description: Controls the blend between the detuned signal and the dry signal. At 0%, no detuning is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Controls the amount of detuning, from -50 cents to +50 cents. Extreme values add more depth or intensity to the chorus-like sound.

params.name: Return Curve
params.description: Determines the trajectory curve when returning to the original pitch. Start Slow values are concave (slower changes to start, speeding up toward the end); Start Fast values are convex (the opposite). At the knob's extremes (Start Slow 5 and Start Fast 5), the pitch will actually overshoot a little before settling on the original pitch.

params.name: Return Time
params.description: Determines how long it takes for the signal to return to normal pitch when the block is bypassed.

params.name: Shift Curve
params.description: Determines the trajectory curve of the pitch shift over time. Start Slow values are concave (slower changes to start, speeding up toward the end); Start Fast values are convex (the opposite). At the knob's extremes (Start Slow 5 and Start Fast 5), the pitch will actually overshoot a little before settling on the target pitch.

params.name: Shift Time
params.description: Determines how long it takes for the signal to ramp up or down to the set pitch when the block is enabled.

params.name: Tracking
params.description: Determines how the poly pitch engine reacts to your playing. Leave this set to "X Stable" (fewest artifacts when pitch shifting complex chords) and only select a different setting if you experience too much latency when playing fast lead lines.

params.description: Controls the speed at which the sustained note or chord fades in.

params.name: Auto EQ
params.description: Determines how much compensation EQ is applied to the sustained signal. If the sustained signal sounds too harsh when pitched up (or dull when pitched down), adjust this setting to taste. The higher the value, the more EQ is applied at the shift end points; when set to 0.0, no compensation EQ is applied.

params.name: Decay
params.description: Controls the speed at which the sustained note or chord fades out after bypassing the effect.

params.name: FX Level
params.description: Controls the level of the sustained signal.

params.name: Interval
params.description: Sets the pitch of the sustained note or chord. TIP: This parameter is especially cool for creating massive drones to play over.

params.name: Mod Depth
params.description: Controls the depth of the built-in modulation.

params.name: Mod Freq
params.description: Controls the speed of the built-in modulation.

params.name: Operation
params.description: Determines what happens to your signal when Poly Sustain is turned on. When set to "Mute All," THE ENTIRE PATH IS MUTED. When set to "Dry Kill," only the sustained signal is heard. When set to "Normal," both the sustained and dry signals are heard. TIP: With Poly Sustain on a parallel path, assign a second stomp switch to toggle between Mute All and Dry Kill.

params.name: Rand Depth
params.description: Higher values increase the randomization of the section of audio being sustained, resulting in a more natural, but less predictable drone.

params.name: Rand Speed
params.description: Controls how fast the randomization wanders.

params.name: Auto EQ

The higher the value, the more EQ is applied at the shift end points; when set to 0.0, no compensation EQ is applied.

params.description: Predetermines the length of the audio to be recorded and looped. To loop an entire 4/4 bar, choose 1/1; to stutter your playing, start with 1/16 or 1/32.

params.name: Sensitivity
params.description: Controls the sensitivity of the compressor's input. Higher values apply more compression.

params.name: Bass
params.description: Adds a 150Hz bass boost to the signal. 0.0 is flat.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a 90Hz low cut (high pass) filter to the signal (6dB/octave).

params.name: Treble
params.description: Adds a 3.5kHz treble boost to the signal. 0.0 is flat.

params.name: Low Cut

params.name: Saturation

params.name: Tape Speed
params.description: Changes both the rate of the modulation applied by the WowFluttr control and the filtering response of the analog tape emulation.

params.name: Texture
params.description: Controls the amount of the NAB tape EQ in the simulated tape path. When Saturation is set to 0.0, the texture is invisible. When Saturation is turned up, the texture will affect the tightness (or looseness) of the distortion.

params.name: Wow/Flutter

effects.name: Rochester Comp

params.name: Attack
params.description: Controls how quickly compression is applied once the signal exceeds the Threshold. Higher values mean a slower attack, which lets the instrument's initial transient sneak through and only compresses the sustained portion of the signal.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Increases the signal's level to compensate for the reduced level that results from compression.

params.name: Knee
params.description: Controls how smoothly compression kicks in. Higher values cause more of a gradual increase in Ratio as the signal approaches the Threshold.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the compressed and dry signals. At 0%, no compressed signal is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. Values in between provide parallel compression.

params.name: Ratio
params.description: Determines how much compression is applied to the signal once it exceeds the Threshold. Higher values mean more compression.

params.name: Release
params.description: Controls how quickly the signal returns to unity gain after it returns below the Threshold.

params.name: Threshold
params.description: Sets the level above which compression is applied. Lower values compress more of the signal; higher values compress only louder parts of the signal.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Controls the amount of distortion applied to the signal. Low Gain and high Level settings are commonly used to tighten up the signal, especially when pushing higher gain amps.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block. Low Gain and high Level settings are commonly used to tighten up the signal, especially when pushing higher gain amps.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of the distortion. Lower values are darker and higher values are brighter.

params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the modulation effect and the dry signal. The most intense phasing happens around 50%.

params.name: Rate
params.description: Controls the speed or rate of the phaser. When set to note values, Speed follows the system tempo.

params.description: Adjusts the decay time of the reverb effect.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Intensity
params.description: Controls the intensity of the modulation. At higher values, you may hear a phaser-like effect within the reverb.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the reverb and the dry signal. At 0%, no reverb is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Modulation
params.description: Controls the amount of modulation applied to the reverb.

params.name: Predelay
params.description: Controls the amount of delay heard before the audible onset of reverb. Can sometimes result in more definition between the dry and effected signals.

params.name: Speed
params.description: Controls the speed of the modulation applied to the reverb.

params.name: Pitch Blend
params.description: Controls how much of Pitch 1 is heard vs. Pitch 2 (set to "Even" by default).

params.name: Damping
params.description: Determines the frequency above which the reverb will be absorbed. For example, if your hall is full of people wearing shimmery astronaut costumes, more high frequencies would be absorbed than if the room were empty.

params.name: Decay
params.description: Adjusts the decay of the reverb (0.1 sec ~ 45.0 sec or Infinity)

params.name: Diffusion
params.description: Controls the amount of smearing between discrete echoes, sometimes resulting in a softer effected signal.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Controls how many times the pitch shifting recirculates through the reverb.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency

params.name: Intensity
params.description: Controls the mix between the pitch-shifted and non-pitch-shifted reverb.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the reverb and the dry signal. At 0%, no reverb is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Type
params.description: Selects the type of shimmer effect applied. "Luster" is more of a traditional, reverb pedal-type shimmer effect with tighter definition in the lustery bits. "Sheen" is more of a lush, studio plugin-type shimmer effect with a massive, sheeny bloom.

params.name: Motion
params.description: Controls the amount of randomization, which can be helpful to minimize any metallic artifacts common in static reverbs. At higher values, can impart a bit of modulation to the effected signal.

params.name: Predelay
params.description: Controls the amount of delay heard before the audible onset of reverb. Can sometimes result in more definition between the dry and effected signals.

params.name: Room Size
params.description: Selects the size of the room (10, 20, or 30 meters).

params.name: Pitch A
params.description: Sets the interval of the first pitch shifter. Set to "Oct Up" for more traditional shimmer sounds; set to "Oct Down" for something a bit creepier. Note that Pitch 1 and Pitch 2 have 0.1 semitone resolution between -1 and +1

params.name: Pitch B
params.description: Sets the interval of the second pitch shifter. Set to "Oct Up" for more traditional shimmer sounds; set to "Oct Down" for something a bit creepier. Note that Pitch 1 and Pitch 2 have 0.1 semitone resolution between -1 and +1

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the loop, letting you remove the looper signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Interval 1
params.description: Sets the pitch of some slices, the likelihood of which is determined by the Pitch parameter (from one octave down to one octave up).

params.name: Interval 2
params.description: Sets the pitch of other slices, the likelihood of which is determined by the Pitch parameter (from -1 octave to +1 octave).

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the loop, letting you remove the looper signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Pitch
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices playing back an interval higher or lower.

params.name: Playback
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Repeat
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices repeating. At 0%, no slices repeat; at 100%, all slices repeat.

params.name: Reverse
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices playing backward. At 0%, all slices play forward; at 100% all slices play backward.

params.name: Seq Drift
params.description: Determines the likelihood of the entire slice sequence changing every time it loops around. When set to 0%, the same sequence repeats forever; when set to 100%, the sequence changes completely every time it loops.

params.name: Seq Length
params.description: Determines the number of slices in the sequence. This can be changed even after recording a loop.

params.name: Shuffle
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices shuffling/reordering. At 0%, the slices never shuffle; at 100%, they're constantly reshuffling.

params.name: Slices
params.description: Changes the number of slices your loop will be chopped into.

params.name: Smoothing
params.description: Higher values apply smoothing between slices and can give a synth-pad type quality, lower values maintain transients. Or set it just high enough to avoid pops and clicks.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Time
params.description: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.

params.name: Cents
params.description: Sets the pitch of the effected signal in cents, from -50.0 to +50.0.

params.name: Interval
params.description: Sets the pitch of the effected signal in semitones, from 2 octaves down to 2 octaves up.

params.name: Level
params.description: Controls the overall level of the block.

params.name: Shift Level
params.description: Controls the level of the pitch-shifted signal.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the pitch-shifted signal and the dry signal. At 0%, no pitch-shifted signal is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Delay
params.description: Delays the pitch-shifted signal slightly. At lower values, it can thicken up your tone or at higher values, it can kind of emulate strumming from a single note.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mode
params.description: Specifies the type of signal sent to the Stereo Imager block. When set to "Mono In", the signal is collapsed to mono before any stereo processing.

params.name: Pan
params.description: Controls the balance between the signal's left and right channels. When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through the block; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through the block.

params.name: Width
params.description: Controls the apparent stereo width of the signal. Values greater than 100% increase the signal's apparent stereo width. Values less than 100% narrow the signal's stereo width. At 0%, the signal is collapsed to mono.

params.name: Balance
params.description: Controls the balance between the signal's left and right channels. When set to L 100, only the left signal is passed through the block; when set to R 100, only the right signal is passed through the block.

params.name: LR In Swap
params.description: When set to "On," swaps the position of left and right channels, so the left signal appears on the right and the right signal appears on the left.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: R Polarity
params.description: Inverts the polarity of the right signal.

params.name: Width
params.description: Controls the apparent stereo width of the signal. When set to "Center," the signal is collapsed to mono. When set to "Wide,", the signal maintains its stereo width.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of overdrive applied to the signal.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of the distortion. Lower values are darker and higher values are brighter.

params.name: Bass
params.description: Controls the low frequency EQ of the distortion.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of distortion applied to the signal.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Treble
params.description: Controls the high frequency EQ of the distortion.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Feedback controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard. At high values, the delay taps may begin to self-oscillate and squeal (perhaps in a good way).

params.name: Filter
params.description: Selects the type of filter applied to the repeats--Low Pass (High Cut), Band Pass, or High Pass (Low Cut).

params.name: Headroom
params.description: Provides up to 12.0 dB of additional headroom.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the repeats, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the delay repeats and the dry signal. At 0%, no repeats are heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Range
params.description: Determines how high the modulation sweeps.

params.name: Resonance
params.description: Controls the resonance or width of the frequency band affected by the filters.

params.name: Shape
params.description: Selects the wave shape of the filter modulation applied to the repeats.

params.name: Rate
params.description: Controls the speed or rate of the modulation applied to the repeats. When set to 0.0, Rate freezes the current filter frequency.

params.name: Start Freq
params.description: Sets the lowest frequency in the sweep modulation.

params.name: Duty Cycle
params.description: Alters the modulation wave shape in differing ways. For example, when Shape is set to "Triangle," 50% is a normal triangle wave and extreme values warp the wave toward a saw down (0%) or saw up (100%) shape. Or with Sine, 50% is a normal sine wave and extreme values warp the wave toward a parabolic down (0%) or parabolic up (100%) shape.

params.name: Time
params.description: Adjusts the length of time before the first repeat. When set to note values, Time follows the system tempo.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the Wah block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the wah effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no wah effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. If the wah effect is a bit strong, consider bringing this down a bit.

params.name: Position
params.description: Adjusts the position or frequency of the wah effect. By default, this is assigned to Expression Pedal 1. Set Min and Max below to restrict the wah's frequency sweep range.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the Wah block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the wah effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no wah effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. If the wah effect is a bit strong, consider bringing this down a bit.

params.name: Position
params.description: Adjusts the position or frequency of the wah effect. By default, this is assigned to Expression Pedal 1. Set Min and Max below to restrict the wah's frequency sweep range.

params.name: Q Trim
params.description: Controls the Q or bandwidth of the effect. Lower values boost a wider frequency band and higher values boost a narrower frequency band.

params.name: Volume Trim
params.description: Emulates the actual pedal's side volume trim knob.

params.name: Bass Cut
params.description: Cuts low end frequencies from the signal before the overdrive circuit.

params.name: Clipping
params.description: Selects the clipping mode. "Up" provides asymmetrical clipping with a bit of compression and saturation. "Center" provides symmetrical clipping with a bit of saturation and high headroom. "Down" is similar to "Center" except with more saturation and lower headroom.

params.name: Gain
params.description: Controls the amount of overdrive applied to the signal.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Treble Cut
params.description: Cuts high end frequencies from the signal after the overdrive circuit.

params.name: Boomerang
params.description: When on, the sequence plays forward, then backward, then forward again, etc. When off, the end of the sequence repeats indefinitely.

params.name: Direction
params.description: Determines the direction of the repeats. "Forward" makes each repeat play back normally. "Reverse" causes repeats to play back in reverse. "Fwd/Rev" alternates between forward and reverse.

params.name: FX Level
params.description: Controls the level of the effected signal.

params.name: First
params.description: Determines the length of the repeats at the beginning of the sequence, that is, the length of repeated audio when the block is first engaged. When set to note values, First (Time) follows the system tempo.

params.name: HP Filter
params.description: Controls the high-pass (low cut) filter frequency for the last step. For example, if set to a higher value, each successive step will filter out more bass until the last step of the sequence.

params.name: LP Filter
params.description: Controls the low-pass (high cut) filter frequency for the last step. For example, if set to a lower value, each successive step will filter out more treble until the last step of the sequence.

params.name: Last
params.description: Determines the length of the repeats at the end of the sequence. If shorter than the First step's time, the sequence will get shorter; if longer than the First step's time, the sequence will get longer. If First and Last are the same time, the sequence length remains constant. When set to note values, Last (Time) follows the system tempo.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Operation
params.description: Determines what happens to your signal when Tesselator is turned on. When set to "Mute All," THE ENTIRE PATH IS MUTED. When set to "Dry Kill," only the effected signal is heard. When set to "Normal," both the effected and dry signals are heard. TIP: With Tesselator on a parallel path, assign a second stomp switch to toggle between Mute All and Dry Kill.

params.name: Pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch shift for the last step in semitones. For example, if set to -12, the last step will be an octave lower than the first step. Disabled unless Ramp is set to "Pitch."

params.name: Ramp
params.description: Determines whether any speed/pitch changes across the sequence reference a static or semitone value. "Speed" sets the target speed of the last step; use the Speed parameter to set the specific value (0% ~ 200% speed). "Pitch" sets the target pitch of the last step; use the Pitch parameter to set the value (-12 ~ +12 semitones).

params.name: Speed
params.description: Sets the speed for the last step in the sequence. For example, if set to 200%, the last step's speed will be twice as fast as the first step and if set to 0%, the last step will appear to stop completely, almost like a glitchy tape stop effect. Disabled unless Ramp is set to "Speed."

params.name: Steps
params.description: Determines how many steps there are in the sequence (1 to 50), with steps in the middle interpolating repeat length, speed/pitch, and/or filter cutoff. For example, if your first step is 100 ms and your last step is 500 ms, each successive step in the sequence will interpolate between 100 ms and 500 ms.

params.name: Attack
params.description: Increases the apparent attack of the signal, providing transient punch and a bit of additional gain.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls the amount of fuzz applied to the signal. Can also affect tone, depending on the Attack knob's setting.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Notch Freq
params.description: Adjusts the frequency at which the Notch Gain boosts or cuts.

params.name: Notch Gain
params.description: Cuts or boosts the signal at the Notch Frequency.

params.name: Thick
params.description: Adds a bit more thickness and low end to the fuzz, particularly if Drive is set lower.

params.name: Fc High
params.description: Sets the high frequency cutoff of the wah filter. Along with Fc Low, sets the frequency range or sweep of the wah.

params.name: Fc Low
params.description: Sets the low frequency cutoff of the wah filter. Along with Fc High, sets the frequency range or sweep of the wah.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the Wah block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the wah effect and the dry signal. At 0%, no wah effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. If the wah effect is a bit strong, consider bringing this down a bit.

params.name: Position
params.description: Adjusts the position or frequency of the wah effect. By default, this is assigned to Expression Pedal 1.

params.name: Center Freq
params.description: Adjusts the frequency around which the boost and cut pivot.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Tilt
params.description: Values above "Flat" boost high frequencies while simultaneously cutting low frequencies; values below "Flat" boost low frequencies while simultaneously cutting high frequencies. Great for quickly making tones a bit brighter or darker with the minimum of fuss.

params.name: Clipping 1
params.description: Selects the clipping mode for Gain 1. "Overdrive" has a touch of drive and compression. "Clean" is less compressed than "Overdrive" and is ideal for boosting your signal into an amp; it's the default setting for Gain 1. "Distortion" provides even more drive and compression.

params.name: Clipping 2
params.description: Selects the clipping mode for Gain 2. "Overdrive" has a touch of drive and compression; it's the default setting for Gain 2. "Clean" is less compressed than "Overdrive" and is ideal for boosting your signal into an amp. "Distortion" provides even more drive and compression.

params.name: Gain 1
params.description: Controls the amount of Gain 1 drive applied to the signal.

params.name: Gain 2
params.description: Controls the amount of Gain 2 drive applied to the signal.

params.name: Gain Mod 1
params.description: The original pedal has different variations available, one with more gain ("Higher").

params.name: Gain Mod 2
params.description: The original pedal has different variations available, one with more gain ("Higher").

params.name: Level 1
params.description: Sets the overall output level of Gain 1.

params.name: Level 2
params.description: Sets the overall output level of Gain 2.

params.name: Presence 1
params.description: Adds a bit more high end sparkle to Gain 1.

params.name: Presence 2
params.description: Adds a bit more high end sparkle to Gain 2.

params.name: Tone 1
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of Gain 1. Lower values are darker and higher values are brighter.

params.name: Tone 2
params.description: Controls the overall tonal balance of Gain 2. Lower values are darker and higher values are brighter.

params.name: Voltage
params.description: The original pedal was designed to be powered by a 9V power supply but could alternatively accommodate 18V, which would provide a bit more headroom. This is especially apparent when Clipping is set to "Boost" and Gain is turned up.

params.name: Wow/Flutter

With Sine, 50% is a normal sine wave and extreme values warp the wave toward a parabolic down (0%) or parabolic up (100%) shape. With Square, 50% is an even square wave, higher values lengthen the signal's on time, and lower values shorten the signal's on time. DutyCycle does not apply to Saw Up or Saw down.

params.description: When on, the sequence plays forward, then backward, then forward again, etc. When off, the end of the sequence repeats indefinitely.

params.name: Direction
params.description: Determines the direction of the repeats. "Forward" makes each repeat play back normally. "Reverse" causes repeats to play back in reverse. "Fwd/Rev" alternates between forward and reverse.

params.name: FX Level
params.description: Controls the level of the effected signal.

params.name: First
params.description: Determines the length of the repeats at the beginning of the sequence, that is, the length of repeated audio when the block is first engaged. When set to note values, First (Time) follows the system tempo.

params.name: HP Filter
params.description: Controls the high-pass (low cut) filter frequency for the last step. For example, if set to a higher value, each successive step will filter out more bass until the last step of the sequence.

params.name: LP Filter
params.description: Controls the low-pass (high cut) filter frequency for the last step. For example, if set to a lower value, each successive step will filter out more treble until the last step of the sequence.

params.name: Last
params.description: Determines the length of the repeats at the end of the sequence. If shorter than the First step's time, the sequence will get shorter; if longer than the First step's time, the sequence will get longer. If First and Last are the same time, the sequence length remains constant. When set to note values, Last (Time) follows the system tempo.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Operation
params.description: Determines what happens to your signal when Tesselator is turned on. When set to "Mute All," THE ENTIRE PATH IS MUTED. When set to "Dry Kill," only the effected signal is heard. When set to "Normal," both the effected and dry signals are heard. TIP: With Tesselator on a parallel path, assign a second stomp switch to toggle between Mute All and Dry Kill.

params.name: Pitch
params.description: Sets the pitch shift for the last step in semitones. For example, if set to -12, the last step will be an octave lower than the first step. Disabled unless Ramp is set to "Pitch."

params.name: Ramp
params.description: Determines whether any speed/pitch changes across the sequence reference a static or semitone value. "Speed" sets the target speed of the last step; use the Speed parameter to set the specific value (0% ~ 200% speed). "Pitch" sets the target pitch of the last step; use the Pitch parameter to set the value (-12 ~ +12 semitones).

params.name: Speed
params.description: Sets the speed for the last step in the sequence. For example, if set to 200%, the last step's speed will be twice as fast as the first step and if set to 0%, the last step will appear to stop completely, almost like a glitchy tape stop effect. Disabled unless Ramp is set to "Speed."

params.name: Steps
params.description: Determines how many steps there are in the sequence (1 to 50), with steps in the middle interpolating repeat length, speed/pitch, and/or filter cutoff. For example, if your first step is 100 ms and your last step is 500 ms, each successive step in the sequence will interpolate between 100 ms and 500 ms.

params.name: Damping
params.description: Determines the frequency above which the reverb will be absorbed. For example, if your hall is full of people wearing fake ocelot jumpsuits, more high frequencies would be absorbed than if the room were empty.

params.name: Decay
params.description: Adjusts the decay of the reverb (0.1 sec ~ 45.0 sec, or Infinity).

params.name: HighCut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: LowCut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the reverb, letting you remove the effected signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the reverb and the dry signal. At 0%, no reverb is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: PreDelay
params.description: Controls the amount of delay heard before the signal enters the plate. Can sometimes result in more definition between the dry and effected signals.

params.name: Intensity
params.description: Controls the amplitude of the modulation, from mild to deep.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the effected signal and the dry signal. At 0%, no effect is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard.

params.name: Warp
params.description: Controls the shape of the LFO. At 0.0, the LFO waveform is a triangle; at +1.0 and -1.0, the waveforms exhibit more chaos, or "warping."

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (or low pass) filter to the loop, letting you remove the looper signal above a certain frequency.

params.name: Interval 1
params.description: Sets the pitch of some slices, the likelihood of which is determined by the Pitch parameter (from one octave down to one octave up).

params.name: Interval 2
params.description: Sets the pitch of other slices, the likelihood of which is determined by the Pitch parameter (from -1 octave to +1 octave).

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (or high pass) filter to the loop, letting you remove the looper signal below a certain frequency.

params.name: Pitch
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices playing back an interval higher or lower.

params.name: Playback
params.description: Sets the overall level of the block.

params.name: Repeat
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices repeating. At 0%, no slices repeat; at 100%, all slices repeat.

params.name: Reverse
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices playing backward. At 0%, all slices play forward; at 100% all slices play backward.

params.name: Seq Drift
params.description: Determines the likelihood of the entire slice sequence changing every time it loops around. When set to 0%, the same sequence repeats forever; when set to 100%, the sequence changes completely every time it loops.

params.name: SeqLength
params.description: Determines the number of slices in the sequence. This can be changed even after recording a loop.

params.name: Shuffle
params.description: Determines the likelihood of slices shuffling/reordering. At 0%, the slices never shuffle; at 100%, they're constantly reshuffling.

params.name: Slices
params.description: Changes the number of slices your loop will be chopped into.

params.name: Smoothing
params.description: Higher values apply smoothing between slices and can give a synth-pad type quality, lower values maintain transients. Or set it just high enough to avoid pops and clicks.

params.name: Speaker Blend
params.description: Controls how much of the woofer speaker is heard vs. the horn speaker. Normally leave this set to "Equal."

params.name: Drive
params.description: Controls how much of the speaker's internal amp is overdriven. At higher values, the speaker imparts more of a gritty sound. Note that the original speaker Vibe Rotary is based on did not have an amplifier, so for the most authentic sound, leave this set to 0.0.

params.name: Fast Speed
params.description: Sets the rotary speed when Speed is set to "Fast." When set to note values, FastSpeed follows the system tempo.

params.name: Headroom

params.name: Level

params.name: Mix

params.name: Ramp Time
params.description: Determines how fast the rotary speed changes when Speed is changed from "Slow" to "Fast" or vice versa.

params.name: Slow Speed
params.description: Sets the rotary speed when Speed is set to "Slow." When set to note values, SlowSpeed follows the system tempo.

params.name: Speed
params.description: Selects Slow or Fast rotary speed. When changing values, the rotary speaker speed gradually changes, based on the RampTime value.

params.name: Bit Depth

params.name: Depth
params.description: Controls the depth or intensity of the pitch modulation applied to the repeats.

params.name: Feedback
params.description: Controls the number of delay repeats. When set to 0%, only one repeat is heard; at 100%, the delay repeats forever.

params.name: Headroom
params.description: Some older rackmount delays' internal signal paths exhibit a bit of grit, especially when placed after a high-gain amp block. Negative values increase the perceived amount of grit; positive values clean things up a bit.

params.name: Rate

params.description: Adjusts the position of the Volume Pedal. By default, this is assigned to Expression Pedal 2.

params.name: Curve
params.description: Sets the Volume Pedal's taper to "Linear" (consistent level change across the pedal's travel) or "Logarithmic" (concave curve, with more control toward the heel and faster changes toward the toe)

params.description: Controls the tonal balance of the triggered oscillator. Higher values provide more harmonics.

params.name: Tone

params.name: Distance
params.description: Sets the distance of the mic from the speaker cone. Choose from 1.00" to 12.00" in 1/4" increments.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter, letting you remove all audio above a certain frequency. May be useful in removing high end harshness.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the Cab. Use to adjust level against the other side of the Cab block.

params.description: Controls the panning of the Cab between the left and right channels. For stereo setups, the Cab block can sound much wider if the two sides are panned opposite of one another ("L 100" and "R 100")

params.name: Position
params.description: Sets the lateral location of the mic in relation to the speaker cone, from center of the speaker to the edge. The "Cap Edge" value may appear in a different location depending on the selected cab.

params.name: Angle
params.description: Sets the angle of the mic relative to the front of the speaker cabinet. 0 degrees is pointing directly at the speaker, 45 degrees is pointing off-axis.

params.name: Delay
params.description: Delays the signal slightly to purposely impart a bit of phase incoherence or at higher values, increase the Cab block's apparent stereo width. A little goes a long way here. When set to "Auto" (all the way left, before 0.0 ms), it approximates the delay through the air when changing the mic Distance parameter.

params.name: Distance
params.description: Sets the distance of the mic from the speaker cone. Choose from 1.00" to 12.00" in 1/4" increments.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Applies a high cut (low pass) filter, letting you remove all audio above a certain frequency. May be useful in removing high end harshness.

params.name: Level
params.description: Sets the overall level of the Cab. Use to adjust level against the other side of the Cab block.

params.name: Low Cut
params.description: Applies a low cut (high pass) filter, letting you remove all audio below a certain frequency. May be useful in removing undesirable low end rumble.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Controls the blend between the incoming “dry” signal and the Cab IR-processed “wet” signal. At 0%, no IR is heard; at 100%, no dry signal is heard. Normally, this should be left at 100%.

params.name: Pan
params.description: Controls the panning of the IR between the left and right channels. For stereo setups, the Cab block can sound much wider if the two sides are panned opposite of one another ("L 100" and "R 100")

params.name: Polarity
params.description: Inverts the polarity of the signal.
